paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: Single vs. multiple platforms as data sources over time. While most of the datasets are collected from a single source, around 2018 researchers are increasingly collecting data from multiple sources (i.e., two or more).
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the number of datasets collected from single versus multiple data sources over time, from 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the year, labeled sequentially from 2012 to 2022, while the vertical axis indicates the number of datasets, ranging from 0 to 100 in increments of 20. Two categories are shown in the legend: "1" (single data source) represented by blue bars, and "2+" (two or more data sources) represented by orange bars. For each year, two bars are displayed side-by-side, with the blue bar consistently taller than the orange bar in most years, indicating that datasets from a single source are more common. In 2012, both bars are nearly negligible, with the blue bar at approximately 1 and the orange bar at 0. From 2013 to 2016, the blue bars remain low (around 1–3), while the orange bars are near zero. Starting in 2017, both bars increase, with the blue bar reaching 25 and the orange bar around 5. In 2018, the blue bar is at 30 and the orange bar at 20. By 2019, the blue bar reaches 45 and the orange bar 20. In 2020, the blue bar rises to 85 and the orange bar to 45. In 2021, the blue bar peaks at 105 and the orange bar at 50. In 2022, the blue bar drops to 30 and the orange bar to 10. The bars are not sorted by value but by chronological order of the years. There is no visual emphasis such as shading or annotation on specific bars. The chart visually supports the caption’s claim that while single-source datasets dominate, there is a noticeable increase in datasets from multiple sources starting around 2018.
